_comment_family: Brittany Signature ships as one file and one cut, so unlike the two
Telegraf packs there is no sibling here for a bare family name to be
confused with - and the file's own name ID 1, its full name and its
typographic family are all the same string. 'Brittany Signature' is
therefore what the file says it is rather than a full name assembled
by hand, which is the same position garet-book is in.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass. A signature hand
has no weight axis to ask along: there is one hand, and asking for a
bold would only invite a browser to smear it.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. They
are spelled exactly as the file spells them - the PostScript one runs
the words together and carries the style on the end, which is the
font's business and not a spelling to be tidied. A name nothing is
installed under is a local() source that can never match and a value
the installer would register the face under while Windows keyed it by
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and here the choice
is unusually consequential: this is a joined signature hand, and
every heavy display cut the other packs in this folder fall through
is the furthest possible thing from it. Impact behind this face would
not be a degraded Re-belle, it would be a different channel.
So the stack stays a hand all the way down. Segoe Script is on every
Windows 10 and 11 and is the nearest joined hand the machine can be
relied on to have; Brush Script MT is the one behind it, on any
machine that has ever had Office; and the generic `cursive` is the
last thing that is still a script rather than a grotesque.
